subject: Request: DPA classification waiver for masked telemetry + subprocessor access matrix
messages:
From: Dara Kim <dara@lunara.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com
Cc: legal@lunara.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline: masked telemetry classification waiver and limited subprocessor access

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited by the latency and the routing controls. Our legal team attached a DPA with a couple of unusual asks we wanted to surface to product/security before we move forward:

- Classification waiver request: they want an explicit carveout that allows Lunara to receive "masked telemetry" (tokens, timestamps, and coarse model selection metadata) for model performance diagnostics. They propose this be non-identifiable and stored for 90 days.
- Subprocessor access matrix: they want a limited list of runtime subprocessors who can receive masked telemetry, plus a more detailed access matrix for those subprocessors.

Files attached: Lunara_DPA_redline_v2.pdf and runtime-access-matrix.xlsx. Can you confirm what product/security would need to approve a limited classification waiver like this and whether the access matrix format works for Redwood?

We'd like to close the procurement review next week if possible.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Dara
Head of Procurement, Lunara AI

From: jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redline: masked telemetry classification waiver and limited subprocessor access

Team — forwarding Lunara's request. High level asks: masked telemetry retention 90d and a named runtime subprocessor matrix.

Quick product questions for the review:
- What exactly will they call "masked telemetry"? From our side this could include prefix tokens stripped of PII, model id, latency buckets, and sampling flags. We need to be explicit.
- Can we enforce masking at ingestion so no unhashed user identifiers ever leave the customer boundary? If yes, how does that affect our diagnostics (loss of root-cause traces)?
- Is 90 days reasonable for our troubleshooting and model regressions cadence, or do we recommend a shorter window with on-demand extended retention via audit?

Olga / Soojin — security signoff needed on:
- Acceptable masking semantics,
- Approved subprocessors and the access matrix format,
- Any contractual language we should ask Legal to add for runtime access revocation and audit rights.

Can we get an internal position by end of day Monday so I can respond to Lunara before their legal call Tuesday?

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Product (Serving)
Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com, soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline: masked telemetry classification waiver and limited subprocessor access

Jonas —

Thanks for the detail. Preliminary security assessment below. Short answer: we can approve a limited, conditional waiver provided a few technical controls and contract clauses are in place.

Key technical controls we need enforced (minimum):
1) Deterministic PII-stripping at ingress: any identifiers (email, user ids) must be hashed with a customer-scoped salt that never leaves the customer's environment. We can integrate hooks to enforce this on private deployments and suggest client-side SDK enforcement for hosted.
2) Token truncation + sampling: full tokens should never be shared; only token prefixes (first N chars) and token length buckets for debugging. Sampling rates must be contractually bounded (e.g., <= 1% of requests, auditable).
3) Aggregation window: 90 days is acceptable if access is read-only and only at aggregated levels; for case-level debugging require DocuSign / escalation and SC-approved temporary extension.
4) Subprocessor gating: runtime subprocessors must be named in an exhibit and must pass our SRE and third-party risk checklist. Any addition requires 30-day notice + right to object.

Contract clauses we need inserted:
- Explicit definition of "masked telemetry" in the DPA (what fields are allowed),
- Audit and revocation rights for Redwood,
- Retention caps and emergency escalation flow for extended retention,
- SLA for access requests (how quickly Lunara can get temporary access for debugging).

On the access matrix: the spreadsheet looks fine structurally, but we need a column for "access enforcement point" (e.g., customer-side masking vs runtime post-process), and "approval owner" (who at Redwood signs off).

If product can confirm which fields they consider necessary for diagnostics and provide an answer on enforcing masking at ingestion (client SDK vs runtime), security can provide a signoff statement to Legal by EOD Tuesday.

-Olga
Olga Petrov
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com, olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline: masked telemetry classification waiver and limited subprocessor access

Folks — product notes below on diagnostics tradeoffs and an implementation proposal.

1) What fields we need (minimal):
- model_id (string),
- model_version (string),
- latency_ms (numeric bucketed),
- input_token_count / output_token_count (numeric buckets),
- truncated input prefix (first 8 bytes of tokens) for reproducing prompt truncation issues,
- coarse error classification (e.g., tokenization_error, generation_timeout).

2) Masking enforcement:
- For hosted customers we can implement an ingress masking microservice in the edge layer so that no unhashed customer identifiers are forwarded to downstream runtime. This is deployable within 3 sprints as an AB-deployable feature.
- For private deployments, we will document the SDK enforcement pattern and provide sample tooling; runtime can expose a toggle but we would prefer ingestion masking to be the canonical control.

3) Retention policy suggestion:
- Default 30 days masked retention for all customers, with explicit contractual allowance for 90 days for named enterprise customers where security signs off. Any extension must be requested via a ticket, logged, and approved by Security.

4) Runtime subprocessors:
- We can publish an exhibit naming current runtime subprocessors (monitoring vendor, metrics pipeline). For new additions, we propose a 30-day notice + objection clause.

Next steps: Jonas, if you agree with the 30-day default + conditional 90-day allowance, I'll draft the exact wording for Legal and an exhibit template for subprocessors. Also will update the access matrix to include "enforcement_point" and "approval_owner" columns.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Product Manager, Serving
Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com
To: Dara Kim <dara@lunara.ai>
Cc: legal@lunara.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com, soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline: masked telemetry classification waiver and limited subprocessor access

Dara — thanks for the patience and details. We're generally aligned and can propose the following position to kick off legal redlines:

1) Definition: Redwood accepts a limited "masked telemetry" carveout defined as: model_id, model_version, latency buckets, token count buckets, truncated token prefixes (first 8 token-bytes), and coarse error tags. No raw prompt text or unhashed user identifiers.
2) Retention: Default masked telemetry retention will be 30 days. For enterprise customers (including Lunara) we can support up to 90 days provided Security signs off and the access is read-only and auditable. Extended retention will require a formal approval ticket and will be logged.
3) Masking enforcement: For hosted customers we will deploy an ingress masking service; for private deployments customer-side SDK enforcement is required. We'll add an "enforcement_point" column to your matrix to show this.
4) Subprocessors: We'll include a runtime subprocessor exhibit. Additions require 30-day notice and Redwood's right to object; subprocessors must pass our SRE and third-party risk checklist.

I'll ask Legal to propose DPA language consistent with the above and include the edited access matrix. Olga and Karthik — thanks for the quick reviews. If Security is comfortable with the conditional wording above, can you confirm an official signoff line so I can share with their counsel tonight?

Best,
Jonas
Director, Product (Serving)
Redwood Inference
